summary: Verified ConCon v0.3.1 fixes for Chrome MV3 extension. Ran Node.js unit test suite: 68/68 tests pass (7 new for concon-check, 4 new for extractor gaps, plus 57 regression tests). Verified all code fixes by inspection: (1) store.loadConversation now restores/rebuilds ledger (line 149: `conv.ledger = row.ledger || updateLedger(null, Array.from(conv.messages.values()))`); (2) panel.js privacy copy corrected — false 'Close the tab' / 'unless you say so' claims removed, IndexedDB reality clearly stated in help overlay; (3) commitment-extract test cases for bare 'I want X', 'I need X', 'I'd like', and expanded conditional hedges all present and passing; (4) concon-check.js correctly enforces doctrine: status='pass' only when coverage==='full' AND unresolvedCount===0 AND contestedCount===0, and formatStatusHeadline never uses 'aligned'/'no drift' language. Shipped zip artifact at /app/frontend/public/concon-extension.zip contains the same fixed sources.
critical_code_review_comments: store.js line 149 ledger restoration fix is logically sound: prefers persisted row.ledger (preserves user-set confirmed/contested/dismissed states) with deterministic rebuild fallback. Correctly addresses the ingest() short-circuit issue on identical text.

concon-check.js doctrine gating is airtight: the coverage!=='full' branch runs before the pass/review decision, so it is structurally impossible for status='pass' with partial coverage. formatStatusHeadline uses 'administratively clean' — carefully avoids 'aligned'/'no drift' claims as required.

panel.js empty-state copy (lines 772, 1009) uses short 'Everything stays on your device. Tap ? for more.' and defers full disclosure to the help overlay (line 789) which has the corrected IndexedDB reality copy. No stale 'Close the tab' / 'unless you say so' strings remain anywhere in the panel source.

Consider adding a dedicated unit test for store.loadConversation's ledger restore path (with a mocked IndexedDB row) so this P0 fix is guarded by CI. Currently the fix is verified only by code inspection.
extension/src/panel/panel.js is 1148+ lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline. Nice-to-have: split renderReport, overlay logic, and DOM composition into separate modules. Not blocking v0.3.1.
test_credentials: n/a — extension has no accounts/auth by doctrine
